Public Participation Information
  In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493,
  2498 and 2499, due to the continuing state of emergency, including masking and social distancing
  directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being held remotely via
  teleconference.  There will not be a physical location for this meeting. Members of the public may
  participate in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 842 9051 8168, Meeting Password: 339794. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 842 9051 8168, Meeting Password: 339794. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  SPECIAL EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  JUNE 6, 2022

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER
A special meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
called to order by CHAIR SCHMITZ at 6:01 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the
Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20.

2.  ROLL CALL
  Committee Members Present:  Brtis, Ciarolla, Griggs, Nilsen, Shinn, Silvano,
  Harik, and Schmitz
  Committee Members Absent:  Martin, Robinson, and Schachter
  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF APRIL 25, 2022
  MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER BRTIS to:
  APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE APRIL 25, 2022, REGULAR
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.
  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN /ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA
  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted that two public comments
  regarding proposed play equipment at Chandler Park had been received via
  email and were forwarded to the Equestrian Committee prior to the start of the
  meeting.

5.  STAFF ITEMS
A.  EQUESTRIAN FACILITY FEES REVIEW UPDATE
  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a verbal overview per written report.
  CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that while a 3% increase sounds like a large increase, the
  highest increase is $30 and the lowest is $2 when looking at the fees.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JUNE 6, 2022
  1
   MEMBER SHINN recommended a larger increase be considered.
  CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that an incremental approach is helpful for the
  constituency but agreed with a larger increase overall.
  MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE REVISIONS TO THE EQUESTRIAN FACILITY FEES AS
  PROPOSED AND RECOMMEND THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSION REVIEW THE REVISIONS TO BE INCORPORATED INTO
  THE FEES AND CHARGES SCHEDULE TO BE APPROVED AND
  ADOPTED BY THE CITY COUNCIL.

  AYES:  Brits, Ciarolla, Griggs, Nielsen, Shinn, Silvano, Harik,
  Schmitz
  ABSENT:  Martin, Robinson, Schacter

  The motion carried.

B.  HORSE TRAINER PERMIT CATEGORY AND FEES UPDATE
  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a verbal overview per written report.

  ACM Davis stated she had received feedback from a member of the public
  regarding the importance of the distinction in Category 2 regarding residency in
  Los Angeles County because those trainers do not use City facilities frequently
  like other local trainers. This feedback was not incorporated in the proposed
  revision and the Committee may wish to consider that distinction.

  MEMBER SILVANO asked why it applied to those who reside outside of Los
  Angeles County as opposed to those outside the City.

  ACM Davis responded that it was understood those trainers do not train
  frequently in the City compared to local trainers.

  MEMBER SILVANO stated that the increases seem high because fees have not
  been raised in a long time but agreed that they should be increased in a similar
  manner as is being done with the fee increases for the Equestrian Facilities at
  Ernie Howlett Park. She also added that that the trainer fees should be higher for
  those who use the facilities more often.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that trainers who use the arenas frequently should pay
  more based on usage but monitoring mechanisms should be considered if we
  remove that distinction.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JUNE 6, 2022
  2
   ACM Davis asked the Committee to clarify the recommended revision to
  Category 2 and for input on the property use charge as proposed.

  MEMBER SHINN was in favor of reducing the Category 2 property use charge to
  $100.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ asked if changing the distinction of trainer’s residency merited
  further review by the City Attorney before moving forward. ACM Davis responded
  that staff would confirm with the City Attorney before moving the item forward to
  the City Council adoption.

  MEMBER SILVANO asked about the payment of the fees. ACM Davis
  responded that all fees are currently collected through the business license
  system but that there may be an option for the permit and usage fees to be
  handled separately. ACM Davis noted that the fees would be effective January 1,
  2023, for trainers who have received their license and permit, which allows time
  to notify the trainers.

  MEMBER SILVANO recommended notifying the trainers of the increases as
  early as possible.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ opened the item up for public comment.

  Community Member Schacter commented that Category B is relied upon by
  dressage trainers from outside the area who use the arena less frequently. She
  stated that she liked the Committee recommendation of $100 as a permit fee for
  a total fee of $550 with usage because as proposed it could impact their decision
  to use the arenas. She also commented that Category B and C should have clear
  distinctions based on the frequency of use of the arenas. She asked if the daily
  fee would continue to be available for trainers.

  ACM Davis responded that a daily fee would remain and is listed within the fees
  and charges schedule.

  Community Member Schacter commented that the daily fee was intended for the
  trainer that used the arenas maybe twice a year. She added that the Category C
  fee could be increased since usage of arenas is more frequent.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ asked the Committee if they were comfortable with staff
  incorporating the changes and forwarding the item to the Park and Activities
  Commission or if they wanted staff to bring the item back for another review
  before forwarding it to the Commission.

  MEMBER SHINN stated she would like to see the item come back to the
  Committee before moving it forward.

  MEMBER SILVANO recommended moving it forward to the Commission to allow
  more time to notify trainers of any approved changes sooner.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JUNE 6, 2022
  3
   MEMBER SHINN stated she would like the day fee clarified. ACM Davis
  responded that staff would look into the day fee to confirm if it is a tax or a City
  established fee.

  There was a consensus to move the item forward to the Park and Activities
  Commission with a review by the City Attorney for future City Council adoption.

C.  REVISED EQUESTRIAN RECOGNITION PROJECTS

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a verbal overview per written report.
  MEMBER SILVANO asked what the initial budget was for the Carol Dean Porter
  project. Supervisor Pinuelas responded it was budgeted at approximately $450.

  MEMBER HARIK moved, seconded by MEMBER GRIGGS, TO:

  APPROVE THE UPDATES TO THE RECOGNITION PROJECTS
  FOR JAN BALL AND CAROL DEAN PORTER USING THE FUNDS
  DONATED TO DATE AS THE BUDGETED AMOUNTS FOR THE
  PROJECTS.

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

D.  PUBLIC RIDING RING RULES UPDATE

  ACM Davis provided a verbal overview per written report.

  ACM Davis stated that two students are allowed per instructor for a total of four
  students and horses allowed at one time in response to CHAIR SCHMITZ
  regarding the number of horses.

  Community Member Schacter commented that the rule limiting trainers to two
  horses was established because some trainers would teach while on a horse
  resulting in three horses per trainer, which didn’t allow for recreational rider use.

  MEMBER HARIK moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO, TO:

  APPROVE THE UPDATE TO THE CITY’S PUBLIC RIDING RING
  RULES AS PROPOSED AND RECOMMEND THE PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES COMMISSION RECOMMEND APPROVAL BY THE
  CITY COUNCIL.
  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

E.  MAYOR'S RIDE DEBRIEF (VERBAL REPORT)

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JUNE 6, 2022
  4
   Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the event.

  MEMBER GRIGGS stated that the event was wonderful and well run. Supervisor
  Pinuelas thanked MEMBER GRIGGS for her assistance at the event.

F.  CHANDLER ARENA – HORSE FACILITY IMPROVEMENTS (VERBAL
  REPORT)

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith provided a brief update regarding the
  progress of the Chandler Arena Renovation.

G.  EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

  There were no questions or comments regarding the log.

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  COMMITTEE REPORTS

A.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

B.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

7.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

A.  AMBASSADOR PROGRAM

  Supervisor Pinuelas noted this item would be brought back at a future meeting.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the Equestrian Committee meeting at 6:58 p.m. to
  the next meeting scheduled to be held on Monday, June 27, 2022, at 7:00 p.m.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  __________________________
  Rosa Pinuelas  Velveth Schmitz, Chair
  Community Services Supervisor

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JUNE 6, 2022
